content.text:
Current routes are semantically inverted: `POST /session` creates a challenge, while `PUT /session` creates the session.

Recommended:

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/session/challenge` | Create admin/login challenge |
| `POST` | `/session/person/challenge` | Create code challenge |
| `POST` | `/session` | Verify solution and create session |
| `GET` | `/session` | Read current session |
| `DELETE` | `/session` | End current session |

`POST`, not `GET`, for challenges: credentials/code require a request body, must not enter URLs, logs, caches, or browser history. Fresh challenge generation also fits `POST`.

I prefer `/session/challenge` over `/session-challenge`; both are clearer than `/session`. It also fits the existing session hierarchy. Current declarations at [routes.php](/home/oem/IdeaProjects/testcenter2/backend/routes.php:44) make `/session` and `/session/person` mean different resources depending on the HTTP method.

Strictly, session creation should also be `POST`, because repeated calls generate/replace tokens and therefore are not idempotent. Existing `PUT /session/admin|login|person` can remain temporarily for compatibility.

Two more important findings:

- Credentials and codes are inserted unencrypted into the returned ALTCHA salt at [SessionController.class.php](/home/oem/IdeaProjects/testcenter2/backend/src/controller/SessionController.class.php:232). The library URL-encodes those values; it does not encrypt them.
- Challenges have no expiration and can be replayed indefinitely. Add a short expiry and preferably one-time-use enforcement.
- No tests currently cover challenge creation/verification routes.

So: rename challenge endpoints, keep them `POST`, and preferably make solved-session creation `POST /session`.
